subject: HelixCare — guaranteed rate escrow and renewal protection request
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Deal Desk <dealdesk@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@helixcare.com>, Procurement <procurement@helixcare.com>
Date: 2027-01-12T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: HelixCare - request: 3yr guaranteed rate w/ escrow and renewal protection

Team,

Quick context: HelixCare is asking for a three year committed agreement. They want two things that are nonstandard for us: a contractual 3-year price lock (no uplift for 36 months) and an uplfit cap on any indexed price increases for renewals. Their procurement lead is also asking for an escrow-backed pricing guarantee to reduce perceived risk on their side.

Proposed commercial terms (customer asks):
- Term: 36 months committed usage
- Starting discount: 15% off our published list for the committed volumes
- Uplift cap: no more than 7% on renewal or mid-term adjustments
- Renewal protection: first automatic renewal inherits capped uplift; subsequent renewals at market
- Escrow: customer requests escrow instrumentation for the discount to be released if we materially change service levels

Attachments: HelixCare_LOU_v1.pdf (term outline), HLX_Economics_3yr.xlsx (unit economics/ARR profile)
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/HLX-2027-1349

Ask: Escalation to leadership for approval. I need a yes/no on the escrow + uplift cap and any guardrails we want to impose (e.g., limit the renewal protection to first renewal only, require SLA credit triggers to move escrow). Customer is sensitive to price volatility; approving this as-is materially helps close a strategic healthcare pilot.

If we approve, next steps: legal to draft escrow clause, finance to confirm P&L impact, and sales to capture final signature.

Thanks,
Priyom
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: HelixCare_LOU_v1.pdf (pdf, 124KB)]
[Attachment: HLX_Economics_3yr.xlsx (xlsx, 52KB)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Deal Desk <dealdesk@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-01-12T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: HelixCare - request: 3yr guaranteed rate w/ escrow and renewal protection

Priyom,

Thanks for the write-up and attachments. A few quick questions from the deal desk/finance lens before we send an approval up the chain:

1) Economics - can you confirm projected blended gross margin over the 36 months with the 15% off list? The attached sheet is helpful but the blended margin by year would be useful for us to quantify runway impact.
2) Escrow mechanism - do they want cash escrow or a neutral third-party escrow that holds a contract-level guarantee? If it's cash we need to evaluate cashflow and any recognition implications.
3) Renewal protection - can we limit the guarantee to the first renewal only? Full perpetual renewal protection exposes us if models/infra costs change materially.

My recommendation to leadership would be: approve a modified package that gives them price stability through year 1 renewal (i.e., protection for the first renewal), reduce uplift cap to 10% to be conservative, and require non-cash escrow via neutral third party or legally scoped SLA triggers.

Cc-ing Vivek for leadership guidance.

- Marissa
Director, Deal Desk

Thanks for flagging this, Priyom. I reviewed the proposal and the economics briefly. I am comfortable approving a tailored program for HelixCare with the following guardrails:

- Approve a 36 month committed term but reduce the starting list discount to 12% (vs requested 15%).
- Uplift cap: approve up to 10% maximum on any renewal or indexed increase (not 7%).
- Renewal protection: limited to the first renewal only. After that, standard renewal terms apply.
- Escrow: approve a neutral third-party escrow that holds an agreement-level guarantee tied to clearly defined SLA breach triggers (legal to draft). No cash escrow hold will be accepted without finance signoff.
- Auto-fallback: include an auto-fallback clause that allows us to route heavy spiky traffic to a compatible model variant if supply or costs change; we will not be forced into unprofitable capacity.

Condition: final approval dependent on finance signoff confirming blended margin >= 38% over the three years after the adjusted discount, and legal redlines to the escrow and renewal protection language. Jordan, please coordinate finance review; Laura, please pick up legal redlines.

Priyom - once legal/finance confirm, you have my signoff to proceed with final commercial docs.

Vivek
VP, Revenue Operations

Team,

Legal reviewed the proposed LOI and flagged a few redlines. I attached a marked-up draft (HelixCare_Redlines_0108.pdf). Key legal points:

1) Escrow - we will agree to a neutral third-party escrow mechanism that holds a contractual declaration, not customer cash, unless finance approves. The escrow will only be releasable on explicit SLA breach or mutual written agreement. We must avoid unconditional cash-hold constructs.
2) Uplift cap language must include objective triggers and a clear calculation formula tied to our published list (so there is no subjective re-pricing).
3) Renewal protection must be time-boxed to the first renewal and should include a materiality carve-out for regulatory or substantial infrastructure cost shocks.
4) Add an auto-fallback operational clause for model variants and capacity shortages; this will protect performance and limits our exposure.

I can transform the redlines into a DocuSign-ready agreement once finance confirms the margin and the commercial team confirms the final discount.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: HelixCare_Redlines_0108.pdf (pdf, 86KB)]

- Starting discount: 12% off list (leadership counter)
